title: Enforce a hard maxTokens budget in lore context; add a separate exact-read op for proof evidence
description:
lore context can retain a target larger than maxTokens while marking the result truncated -- current behaviour, not a new failure, but it means a budget is advisory rather than enforced. See LCLI-203 for the existing documented semantics of --max-tokens (omitting it applies no cap; this task is about what happens when it IS supplied and the target still exceeds it).

Proposed: an explicit hard output budget with omitted-record/field metadata, and a separate exact-read operation for proof evidence.

Cross-repo note: the Quest-side half (field and note selection on task view) has already been routed to quest-cli by opum-agent. This task is scoped to Lore's side only.

Source: 2026-09-13 proof-graph inspection (Lore 0.6.0, Quest 0.6.0), read-only against production, recorded as OPAG-120 on opum-agent.

acceptanceCriteria.text: lore context enforces --max-tokens as a hard ceiling: output never exceeds the specified budget
When records/fields are omitted to fit the budget, metadata names what was omitted (record ids and/or fields)
A separate command or flag provides an exact, untruncated read of specific proof evidence, bypassing the token budget entirely
LCLI-203's existing --max-tokens documentation is reconciled with the new hard-budget behavior rather than left contradictory

implementationNotes:
SHARED SHAPE AGREED WITH QUEST-CLI, 2026-09-14. Recorded here because until now this agreement lived
almost entirely in cross-session message traffic, which is not a record. Quest has landed their half
as decision record DEC-3 (`quest decision view DEC-3` in quest-cli's workspace, their PR #79).
LORE STILL OWES A MATCHING RECORD -- write it when this task starts, then exchange record ids with
quest-cli so the two cross-link.

WHY THE TWO TASKS ARE ONE PROBLEM. opum-agent ruled LCLI-478 and quest's QCLI-276 must be designed
together, and quest-cli independently reached the same conclusion before either of us designed
anything. One sentence covers both: A CONSUMER CANNOT ASK FOR PART OF A THING, SO IT TAKES ALL OF IT
OR NOTHING, AND "ALL OF IT" IS UNBOUNDED. Lore's `context` can retain a target larger than maxTokens
and merely mark the result truncated; quest's `task view` always returns the full record and has a
probe task past 1M characters of implementationNotes.

=== THE THREE SEMANTICS. THESE ARE THE AGREEMENT. BOTH PRODUCTS MUST MATCH ON ALL THREE. ===

1. PROJECTION IS OPT-IN AND ADDITIVE. Absent means everything, so today's output is byte-for-byte
   unchanged for every existing caller.

2. A SUPPLIED BOUND IS ENFORCED, NEVER ADVISORY. This is the half to hold hardest, and it is the
   whole defect on lore's side: an advisory budget is the release's own failure mode in another
   costume -- the caller asked for a guarantee and received a suggestion, with no way to tell which
   they got.

3. OMISSION IS REPORTED, NEVER INFERRED. Whatever is dropped, the response SAYS what it dropped. A
   consumer must never have to diff against a full fetch to discover it received a partial one.
   REFINEMENT THAT QUEST ADOPTED VERBATIM AND LORE MUST HONOUR TOO: the omission marker is present
   whenever projection is ACTIVE, including when nothing was omitted (a literal zero) -- not only
   when something was. If it appears only on a capped response, its ABSENCE is ambiguous between
   "nothing was omitted" and "a version that does not report omission", which is the same defect one
   layer down: a marker that cannot announce its own applicability. It costs one integer.

=== WHAT MAY LEGITIMATELY DIFFER, STATED AS A DECISION SO NOBODY READS IT AS DRIFT ===

The flag SPELLING, the UNIT, and the GRANULARITY. Quest bounds by RECORD COUNT (number of notes);
lore bounds by TOKENS across an assembled pack. Those are DIFFERENT KINDS OF BOUND -- a per-field cap
versus a whole-pack budget -- not the same bound in different units, and forcing one spelling to look
consistent would be its own small lie. A consumer learns the three semantics once and then reads each
tool's own flag list. That is a weaker promise than "identical shape" and it is the true one.

=== QUEST'S SIDE, AS LANDED IN DEC-3 (for reference; do not re-derive) ===

 - Scoped NARROWER than a general field-projection DSL, on evidence: their unbounded growth is
   specifically `implementationNotes` and `comments`, not the record as a whole. So `--max-notes N`
   (possibly `--since <ISO>` as a second selector) rather than a column DSL. A plain `--fields a,b,c`
   layers on additively later if a pain point ever appears; there is none today.
 - `notesOmitted: <count>` as a sibling of the shortened array, always present when projection is
   active.
 - Units: record-count.
 - THEIR DEFAULT ALREADY IS THE EXACT READ, so they need no separately-named exact operation --
   projection is purely additive on top of an unbounded default.

=== LORE'S SIDE, STILL TO DESIGN -- AND ONE PIECE IS STRUCTURALLY OURS ALONE ===

`lore context` ASSEMBLES by default and is LOSSY BY DESIGN (selection, ordering, truncation). So
"give me this record verbatim" genuinely is a DIFFERENT OPERATION here, not a flag on the same one --
unlike quest, whose default is already exact. LCLI-478's "separate exact-read op for proof evidence"
is therefore real work on our side and correctly has no counterpart on theirs. A bounded read and an
exact read must be different operations with different names; collapsing them into one operation with
a flag makes the caller who needs fidelity and the caller who needs cheapness share a code path, and
one of them loses.

DEC-3 records that lore-side detail as PENDING, explicitly not absent-by-decision, so a reader of
DEC-3 alone cannot conclude lore declined it. Whichever of us lands second must preserve the same
courtesy in reverse.

See LCLI-203 for the existing documented semantics of --max-tokens (omitting it applies no cap; this
task is about what happens when it IS supplied and the target still exceeds it).

STATUS: NOT BLOCKED ANY MORE ON THE AGREEMENT ITSELF -- the three semantics above are settled and
quest's half is recorded. What remains is lore's own design and implementation. Do not re-open the
three semantics without telling quest-cli; if lore's write-up surfaces something that breaks one,
say so and reopen it jointly rather than diverging quietly.
